territorial_scope.description: Adds a chapter to California's Business and Professions Code, applying within the state and enforced by state and local officials.

evidence.quote: Chapter 40 (commencing with Section 22949.85) is added to Division 8 of the Business and Professions Code, to read:

summary.short: California SB 384 proposed bill would prohibit selling, licensing, providing or using a price-setting algorithm that processes competitors' nonpublic input data to set prices, supply levels or rents, if two or more competitors are expected to use it. Enforced by civil actions. No effective date is stated.
summary.long: Proposed Business and Professions Code § 22949.85 (SB 384) would prohibit selling, licensing, providing or using a price-setting algorithm, with intent or reasonable expectation that two or more competitors in the same market use it, if the person knows or should know it processes nonpublic input data to set a price or supply level for goods or services, or a rent or occupancy level for rental property. Users have an affirmative defense if they exercise reasonable due diligence, including written assurances from the provider that the algorithm does not process nonpublic input data. Providers face a separate violation per authorized user or licensee; users face a separate violation for each calendar month of use. The Attorney General, a district attorney, or a city attorney or county counsel may sue for actual damages, injunctive relief, restitution or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation, with attorney's fees for prevailing public plaintiffs. Conflicting contracts are void to that extent, and the section does not limit antitrust laws. Definitions cover artificial intelligence, nonpublic input data, price-setting algorithms and competitors. No effective date is stated.

thresholds.variable_text: number of competitors using the same price-setting algorithm
thresholds.value_text: two or more competitors in the same market
thresholds.measurement: Number of competitors (persons or business entities offering similar or substitutable goods, services or real property for lease in the same relevant market to the same or overlapping customer base) that use, or are intended or reasonably expected to use, the algorithm
thresholds.consequence: The prohibition in subdivision (a) applies only where the algorithm is sold, licensed, provided or used with the intent or reasonable expectation that two or more competitors will use it.
thresholds.conditions: Competitors are defined in subdivision (g)(5) as two or more persons or business entities offering similar or substitutable goods, services or real property in the same relevant market to the same or overlapping customer base; the algorithm must also process nonpublic input data to set a price, supply, rent or occupancy level.

evidence.quote: with the intent or reasonable expectation that it be used by two or more competitors in the same market

thresholds.variable_text: age of input data: time between collection and use or distribution of the price-setting algorithm
thresholds.value_text: more than one year before the use or distribution of the price-setting algorithm
thresholds.measurement: Time elapsed between the date the input data was collected and the date of use or distribution of the price-setting algorithm
thresholds.consequence: Data collected more than one year before use or distribution is excluded from the definition of nonpublic input data, so it does not bring the algorithm within the prohibition in subdivision (a).
thresholds.conditions: Applies only to data that is confidential, nonpublic and sensitive information of competitors; the one-year limit is part of the definition of nonpublic input data in subdivision (g)(3).

evidence.quote: but does not include data that was collected more than one year before the use or distribution of the price-setting algorithm
